pr_title: fix: Return largest non-NaN value for `max()` on sorted float arrays if it exists instead of NaN
pr_body:
Fixes https://github.com/pola-rs/polars/issues/12931.

This PR uses a binary search to find non-NaN values for the sorted max/arg_max on floats (if they exist). In the case where all non-null values are NaNs, then the result will be NaN (note the result for all-null is still null).

Part of the binary search code was refactored and moved from `polars-ops` to `polars-core` to support this.

issue_context.title: min/max incorrectly can return nan on sorted arrays
issue_context.body:
Reproduction:

```python
s = pl.Series([1.0, float('nan')])
print(s.max(), s.sort().max())
```

This prints `1.0 nan`.


This is due to the optimization that we pick the first/last element for min/max on sorted arrays.
comments:
I just hit this.

While trying to understand how polars deals with nans and nulls in computing quantiles, I happened to find 

https://docs.pola.rs/docs/python/dev/reference/expressions/api/polars.Expr.nan_max.html

which documents that "This differs from numpy’s nanmax as numpy defaults to propagating NaN values, whereas polars defaults to ignoring them." I found that pleasantly surprising, and then immediately found it to be wrong. Took a while to understand it had to do with my sorting the series. 

This kind of breakage in invariants can be hard to debug, though I still think P-medium sounds about right.

review_comments: We need this for now because binary search does not yet work for arrays sorted with nulls last (https://github.com/pola-rs/polars/issues/15045)
